name: Elamites
summary: One of the oldest civilisations in the world, centred on Susa (Shushan) in south-western Iran. Elam's king Chedorlaomer raided Canaan in Abraham's day. Later, Daniel saw a vision 'in Shushan the palace, which is in the province of Elam', and Elamites were in the Pentecost crowd.
name_meaning: Probably from the Akkadian Elamtu, 'highland', for the Zagros uplands east of Mesopotamia.

origin.account: Elam is listed as the firstborn of Shem. Historically Elam was a civilisation of Susiana (the plain of Susa) and Anshan (in the Fars highlands) from before 3000 BC, with its own writing (Proto-Elamite, then Linear Elamite). Its language is unrelated to any known language.

lineage.notes: A Semite by Genesis's genealogy, though the Elamite language is not Semitic. The Table of Nations groups peoples by geography and politics as well as by language. Several Israelites in Ezra and Nehemiah also bear the name Elam.

homeland.region: Elam — Khuzestan plain and the south-western Zagros
homeland.description: The low, river-watered plain of Susa (continuous with Mesopotamia) and the highland region of Anshan to the south-east. Elamites were famous archers: 'I will break the bow of Elam, the chief of their might.'
homeland.modern_location: Khuzestan and Fars provinces, south-western Iran.

places.name: Shushan (Susa)
places.note: Elam's capital; later Persian royal city.

places.name: River Ulai
places.note: Where Daniel saw the ram and goat.

places.name: Anshan
places.note: Highland capital; Cyrus' ancestors were 'kings of Anshan' (not named in the Bible).

places.name: Chogha Zanbil
places.note: Elamite ziggurat of the 13th century BC (not named in the Bible).

timeline.event: Susa is founded (c. 4000 BC) and Proto-Elamite writing appears.
Chedorlaomer king of Elam leads four kings against the cities of the plain and takes Lot; Abram defeats him.
Elamite king Shutruk-Nakhunte carries the Code of Hammurabi stele off to Susa (where it was found in 1901).
Elamite archers are listed in Assyria's army against Jerusalem.
Ashurbanipal of Assyria sacks Susa; Elamites are deported to Samaria.
Jeremiah prophesies against Elam: 'I will scatter them toward all those winds… But it shall come to pass in the latter days, that I will bring again the captivity of Elam.'
Elam becomes the heart of the Persian empire; Susa is a royal capital.
Elamites among the crowd at Pentecost.

religion.practices: Temple religion with ziggurats (such as Chogha Zanbil). The Bible records no Elamite religious practices.

importance: Elam spans the whole Bible story. It is the first foreign power to invade Canaan in Genesis (Chedorlaomer), and its people are among the first hearers of the gospel at Pentecost. Jeremiah's oracle ends with restoration: judgement is not God's last word even for distant nations. Its capital Susa is the setting of Daniel 8, Nehemiah 1 and the whole book of Esther.

impact.how: His rescue of Lot led to his meeting with Melchizedek.
Received the vision of the ram and the he-goat at Shushan by the Ulai.
Elamites heard 'the wonderful works of God' in their own language.

notable_people.name: Chedorlaomer
notable_people.role: King of Elam in Abram's day

key_verses.text: And it came to pass in the days of Amraphel king of Shinar, Arioch king of Ellasar, Chedorlaomer king of Elam, and Tidal king of nations;
But it shall come to pass in the latter days, that I will bring again the captivity of Elam, saith the LORD.
And I saw in a vision; and it came to pass, when I saw, that I was at Shushan in the palace, which is in the province of Elam; and I saw in a vision, and I was by the river of Ulai.
Parthians, and Medes, and Elamites, and the dwellers in Mesopotamia, and in Judaea, and Cappadocia, in Pontus, and Asia,

fate.summary: Ashurbanipal's sack of Susa (c. 646 BC) broke Elam's independence. It was absorbed into the Persian empire, where Elamite remained an administrative language — most of the Persepolis tablets are in Elamite. Its speakers dwindled over later centuries.

today.summary: There is no Elamite people or language today. Their land is Iran's Khuzestan and Fars provinces. Susa (Shush) is still inhabited and is a UNESCO World Heritage site; a shrine there is traditionally honoured as the Tomb of Daniel.
today.descendants: Absorbed into Iranian populations (Persians, Lurs and others).
today.modern_legacy: Linear Elamite script was largely deciphered in 2020–2022 by François Desset and colleagues.

archaeology.name: Susa excavations
archaeology.location: Louvre, Paris; National Museum of Iran
archaeology.significance: Five millennia of occupation; the Code of Hammurabi and the Persian palace were found here.
